Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
659 AM EDT Sun Aug 30 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 223 AM EDT Sunday...

No significant changes made with this forecast package.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 223 AM EDT Sunday...

1. Cloudy with showers today, and then dry much of Monday.

2. Showers and thunderstorms likely Monday night into Tuesday.

3. A period of showery weather is expected mid to late week, 
with a emphasis on Wednesday night into Thursday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 223 AM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A strong upper trough is diving southwards across Quebec 
Province, but the attendant surface low is far northeast of our 
area. A stretched out frontal boundary will sag southwards while a 
tongue of Pacific moisture rounds an upper ridge axis across the 
central US as we approach dawn. Southwest to west flow against the 
frontal boundary will produce intervals of showers, one along the 
international border this morning, and then more widespread activity 
this afternoon and evening. Convection this afternoon will likely be 
short. There's about 500 J/kg of CAPE, but the equilibrium levels 
will barely make it above -20 C. It will be tough to generate much 
cloud ice. So thunderstorms should be fairly scarce.

Precipitation will decline with sunset as the front pushes south and 
daytime heating ends. High pressure will begin to nose in with 
somewhat cooler air behind the front. A seasonable night of mid 40s 
to mid 50s is expected with dry, pleasant conditions much of Monday. 
Towards the end of Monday, precipitation will approach from the 
southwest.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Upper troughing will continue to dominate far eastern 
Canada, and this northwest flow will continue to prevent a surge of 
warm air from reaching this area. A sluggish warm front will slowly 
shift northeast while mid-level moisture moves northwest to 
southeast over the hump of a 500mb ridge axis extending into James 
Bay. So we'll observe precipitation grazing the region Monday night, 
with the highest rain chances across southern St. Lawrence County, 
and then these rain chances slowly eke northeast Tuesday morning 
into the afternoon. There remains some uncertainty with the 
placement of precipitation. The mid-level moisture could be the 
remnants of convection in the Great Lakes region, and where exactly 
the quasi-stationary front is located will play a large role in 
deciding the focus of heavier rain. Guidance is slightly farther 
northeast this evening, but not by much. Most atmospheric 
instability will be aloft Tuesday. Near surface conditions will be 
mostly stable, and so any storm activity will be garden variety.

KEY MESSAGE 3: During the middle and end of the week, an upper level 
trough will gradually shunt a ridge over the Midwest and Mid-
Atlantic to the south, preventing any heat from building into the 
region. The last of a couple ridge runner type features will move 
through Wednesday night into Thursday, likely bringing an area of 
heavy rain with convective enhancement from elevated instability. 
The warm sector will not be fully established over the area so 
limited surface instability should limit the threat for severe 
weather. However, increasing PWATs and good dynamics will cause an 
axis of heavy rain to develop, though its exact placement is still 
uncertain. The flood threat looks low at this point but will 
continue to be watched. For any flash flooding to occur, the band on 
Wednesday night into Thursday would likely have to occur in the 
exact location as the heavier bands in the beginning of the week for 
a chance. NBM probabilities of 2+ inches of rain are up to around 20 
percent for southern Vermont, the part of the region that has the 
highest probability of seeing the heaviest rain. GEFS 25th-75th 
percentiles range from a quarter to three quarters of an inch at 
this time, which does neglect localized higher amounts due to 
convection. However, trends still continue to prog the best moisture 
and forcing to our southwest. Brief high pressure will nudge in form 
the northwest late Thursday into Friday with seasonable conditions. 
Trends have begun to take more of a wet turn from previous forecasts 
for next weekend, with our Wed/Thu system occluding off the Canadian 
Maritimes, keeping cyclonic flow over and shower chances over our 
area.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 12Z Monday...Prevailing VFR conditions are expected to
continue at all terminals through the next 18 hours. A cold front
will sink south from Quebec with showers already across northern New
York and portions of northern Vermont. Shower chances and 
confidence of rain over northern terminals including 
MSS/EFK/BTV/SLK/PBG will increase by 18Z with perhaps some brief
heavier downpours that could lead to MVFR vsbys reductions. A 
few isolated thunderstorms will also be possible between 18Z-22Z
in the vicinity of the aforementioned terminals, but confidence
in terminal thunderstorms are low at this time, and thus have
not included thunder in any TAF lines. Should a thunderstorm 
pass over a terminal, MVFR/IFR vsbys will be possible with 
changeable winds. Have generally only used PROB30 for rain 
shower vsby reductions this afternoon at this time. Winds around
10-15 knots will shift from the south to the southwest this 
morning and then west throughout the day as the cold front moves
south. A few gusts around 15-20 MPH will be possible as the 
front passes through each terminal, mainly at MSS/BTV. Showers 
will taper off towards 00Z, with increasing confidence in patchy
fog at the climo favored terminals closer to 06Z tonight. 
Should any terminal receive rain, especially if close to 22- 
00Z, fog chances will increase.

Outlook...

Monday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Tuesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Wednesday: MVFR. Likely SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Likely
SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Thursday: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Chance SHRA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
